data.title: A2 Progress Check
data.description: A second mixed grammar check to measure progress and confirm whether the learner is working securely at CEFR A2 level.

sections.explain: Present simple questions use 'do/does' + subject + base verb: 'Where do you live?'. 'Where you live' has no auxiliary, and 'do you lives' wrongly adds '-s'.

words.word: Where you live?
Where do you lives?
Where do you live?

sections.explain: Frequency adverbs like 'always' go before the main verb: 'always arrives'. Placing it after the verb is unusual, and 'always arrive' misses the '-s'.

words.word: He always arrives early.
He arrives always early.
He always arrive early.

sections.explain: 'So' introduces a result: 'I was tired, so I went to bed'. 'Because' introduces a cause (reversed here), and 'so that' expresses purpose.

words.word: I was tired, because I went to bed.
I was tired, so that I went to bed.
I was tired, so I went to bed.

sections.explain: After time words like 'when', use the present simple for the future: 'when I arrive'. Don't use 'will' after 'when' or the bare -ing form.

words.word: I'll call you when I will arrive.
I'll call you when I arriving.
I'll call you when I arrive.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence about a past habit.
sections.summary: A2 · Past Habits: used to / would
sections.explain: 'Used to' + base verb describes a past habit: 'used to play'. The correct form is 'used' (with -d) + base verb, not '-ing'.

words.word: I used to play tennis every weekend.
I used to playing tennis every weekend.
I use to play tennis every weekend.

sections.explain: The negative prefix for 'possible' is 'im-': 'impossible'. 'un-' and 'dis-' are not used with 'possible'.

words.word: It is unpossible to finish today.
It is dispossible to finish today.
It is impossible to finish today.

sections.explain: Present continuous is 'are' + -ing: 'are having'. 'are have' uses the base verb, and 'they having' omits 'are'.

words.word: They are having dinner right now.
They are have dinner right now.
They having dinner right now.

sections.explain: 'Good' has an irregular superlative: 'the best'. 'most best' doubles the superlative, and 'goodest' is not a word.

words.word: This is the most best film I have ever seen.
This is the best film I have ever seen.
This is the goodest film I have ever seen.

sections.explain: The zero conditional states a general fact with present simple in both clauses: 'If you heat ice, it melts'. Never add 'will'.

words.word: If you heat ice, it will melts.
If you will heat ice, it melts.
If you heat ice, it melts.

sections.explain: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'decided to leave'. 'decided leaving' and 'decided to leaving' are incorrect.

words.word: She decided to leaving early.
She decided to leave early.
She decided leaving early.
